parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the reported sink is fgets at line 16; fgets reads raw bytes and does not interpret format specifiers, so %n or other format strings cannot influence program control flow. Moreover, the buffer read by fgets is never passed to any function that could execute commands (no system(), exec*, popen(), etc.), eliminating the possibility of OS command injection. Thus there is no untrusted-to-dangerous-operation path. The claim of arbitrary writes via %n in fgets is incorrect.
